passage:
The park built a bee hotel using bamboo tubes and small wooden holes. A sign explained that it was for solitary bees, not honeybees.
Some visitors were afraid. They thought all bees lived in large groups and attacked people. A park worker explained that many solitary bees are gentle and important for pollination.
Students visited the bee hotel for biology class. They watched small bees enter the holes carrying bits of plant material.
The bee hotel changed their idea of insects. Not every bee is a honey maker, and not every buzzing insect is a danger.
Understanding nature often begins by learning that common names hide many different lives.
